summary: Group append at 41e5e867a3: the full Linux preflight (33 gates passed, actionlint skipped) and the Intel x86_64 macOS native preflight (3 gates) passed on the committed tree, including every group, consumer, and writer-exclusion test. Windows CI also passed 1,444 Cargo tests with three ignored on synthetic merge 829d9143a2, whose tree equals the candidate. Every byte prefix of both consumer groups loads to a provider-valid request; writer takeover is sampled at line boundaries and every 13th byte. Line faults are injected, and child kills land between system calls. Five controls on uncommitted pre-commit trees were rejected. Kills inside a write system call, real ENOSPC, EIO, power loss, Windows PTY, and the rest of the crash matrix remain.

results.behavior: session::manager::group::tests' 9 tests passed in the Linux and Intel macOS rust gates at the candidate; group_writer_child is the kill test's child entry point and returns at once in the parent run. A group writes the lines its single appends write, chained from the leaf; a failed check (missing, not editable, off-branch target) and an empty group write and keep nothing. Every byte prefix of the model-switch and recovery-omission groups is loaded and checked against the projection of the entries it holds and a request bake_ai transform_messages leaves provider-valid. Takeover is sampled, not exhaustive: only at each line boundary and at every 13th byte is the prefix reopened as a writer and appended to, and that append starts its own line. Faults are injected at the durable::append_lines boundary through a cfg(test) seam (refused, torn after 0 and 17 bytes, unsynced, and torn after the whole JSON) at each line of a group; the bytes written are real, and the seam panics if its own write or sync fails. No real ENOSPC or EIO was produced. Counts describe Cargo tests.

a_writer_killed_between_group_lines_leaves_a_loadable_prefix passed on Linux and Intel macOS: a child writer process re-running the test binary is killed with Child::kill while it holds a three-line omission group after 0, 1, and 2 synced lines, and after 1 synced line plus 20 bytes of the next line that it wrote and synced through the seam. The parent asserts the child was still running and ended by SIGKILL, not by its watchdog (exit 3) or a returned write (exit 4); the file loads to the synced lines, rebuilds a provider-valid request, and is taken over by the next writer. These are controlled partial-write kills: the child waits after its own write and sync, so each kill lands between system calls, not inside a write system call. The same test also passed native Windows CI with its exit code 1 check; see windows-group-and-writer.

agent_session::control_tests and agent_session::recovery_tests passed on Linux and Intel macOS (53 tests, which with the group tests make the 62 focused tests in each rust log): set_model writes the model and level as one group and applies nothing unless the model line is known synced, including an unsynced level line a reader sees but the session does not apply; a new session's model and level fail creation at line 1 and keep the prefix; a recovery omission writes tool-result edits before the attempt's, projects as Pi's order when complete, and on a torn or unsynced line publishes only its known synced prefix, stops a retry before its request, and in overflow recovery makes no compaction request; later prompts are refused and the bytes are unchanged after shutdown. Failures are injected through the same seam. Counts describe Cargo tests.

writer_exclusion.rs's 12 tests, unchanged since the 2026-10-14 storage record (same sha256), passed in the Intel macOS rust gate at this candidate, including takeover from a killed and from an exited holder process, and on Linux. This is macOS evidence for this candidate only; it does not change the earlier record.
Group append, the child-kill test, and the consumers on Windows, including the Windows exit code of a killed child and lock takeover after the kill.

negativeControls.defect: In recovery.rs, removed targets.rotate_left(1), so the attempt's edit is written first as Pi writes it.
negativeControls.assertion: a_recovery_omission_is_one_group_projecting_as_pi failed on the file order and a_partly_written_omission_stops_and_shows_what_the_file_holds on the first durable target (0 passed, 2 failed; exit 101). The restored run passed both (exit 0); this earlier script did not print a hash check.

negativeControls.defect: In group_tests.rs, dropped the child's watchdog sleep, so the child exits on its own with code 3 before the parent's kill.
negativeControls.assertion: assert_killed failed: the writer child was not ended by the parent's kill: exit status: 3 (0 passed, 1 failed; exit 101). Restored byte for byte (sha256sum -c); the restored run passed.

negativeControls.defect: In recovery.rs, filtered out the prefix projection, so a failed omission publishes nothing.
negativeControls.assertion: a_failed_overflow_omission_publishes_its_prefix_and_requests_nothing and a_partly_written_omission_stops_and_shows_what_the_file_holds failed on the transcript (0 passed, 2 failed; exit 101). Restored byte for byte (sha256sum -c); the restored run passed.

negativeControls.defect: In durable.rs, made the Tear seam write through a read-only handle, so the seam's own write really fails.
negativeControls.assertion: a_failed_write_at_each_line_keeps_the_written_prefix panicked with test seam: real write failed after 0 bytes: Bad file descriptor, rather than reporting an injected Torn (0 passed, 1 failed; exit 101). Restored byte for byte (sha256sum -c); the restored run passed.

negativeControls.defect: In group.rs, kept the whole group in memory after a failed line instead of the known synced prefix.
negativeControls.assertion: a_readable_failed_line_is_not_in_the_known_synced_prefix and an_unsynced_level_line_is_not_applied failed (0 passed, 2 failed; exit 101). Restored byte for byte (sha256sum -c); the restored run passed.

missingEvidence.reason: Faults are injected at the append_lines boundary and kills are controlled partial-write kills between system calls; no real device error or power cut was produced.

missingEvidence.what: Exhaustive takeover at every byte prefix
missingEvidence.reason: Every byte prefix is loaded and checked, but writer takeover runs only at line boundaries and every 13th byte.

missingEvidence.what: A failed check inside a recovery omission
missingEvidence.reason: omit_recovery_attempt runs append_group inside the write boundary, so a check error (EntryNotFound, NotOnActiveBranch, NotEditable) writes nothing but records the session's gap and stops the session. This is intended and documented; its targets come from the branch just written, no realistic path to it was found, and no test triggers it.

missingEvidence.what: Fault on the unflushed create-then-group path
missingEvidence.reason: Creating the file with earlier entries and then appending the group has no fault test; it is reachable only after an earlier failed flush, which already leaves a gap.

missingEvidence.what: Reconciling an unsynced or whole-JSON torn line
missingEvidence.reason: The manager keeps the known synced prefix while an immediate reopen may read one entry more; tests show the difference, and nothing reconciles the two views within a run.
